item.description: Enterprise agentic AI systems exchange contextual information across functional modules, creating governance challenges when information crosses operational and organizational boundaries. item.description: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly employ reflection mechanisms to inspect their own outputs, identify potential errors, reconsider intermediate decisions, and improve subsequent responses. item.title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
item.description: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. item.title: Fare Calculation Methodology in Automated Public Transport Payment Systems: Zoning, Per-kilometer, and Adaptive Tariffs
item.description: The purpose of the research is to develop proposals for tariff setting in automated fare collection systems for public transport. The work focuses on a critical analysis of the zonal fare model currently operating in the Leningrad region. The study analyzed 760 routes in the Leningrad region. item.title: Strategic Evaluation and Implementation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Price Volatility in the Steel Commodity Market: A Comparative Study with the Foreign Exchange Market for Commercial Decision-Making
item.description: This study aimed to implement and strategically compare machine-learning and deep-learning models for predicting price volatility in the Iranian steel commodity market and the EUR/USD foreign-exchange market and to evaluate their usefulness for commercial decision-making. This applied-developmental study used a descriptive-analytical design based on secondary time-series data from January 2019 to January 2024. item.title: From reproducibility to comparability in computational photochemistry: lessons from the PhotoChem explorer prototype
item.description: We present the PhotoChem Explorer (PCE) prototype, a proof-of-concept web-based platform that represents computational photochemistry studies of gas-phase molecules in a structured and queryable form. item.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
item.description: Artificial intelligence has become a strategic technology whose development requires coordinated institutional, regulatory, ethical, and infrastructural governance. This study evaluated the capacity of Iran’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to support responsible AI governance by reconstructing its underlying program theory and examining the coherence of its implementation architecture. item.title: A roadmap for polymer informatics superintelligence
item.description: Polymer informatics has matured from isolated property-prediction studies into an integrated discipline that couples data, models, and decision-making across the polymer design cycle. Yet it still falls short of a true intelligent system capable of inverse design on demand, causal reasoning across chemistry, processing, and performance, and closed-loop autonomous experimentation. item.title: NeuroImgAgent: a multi-agent platform for cross-species fMRI analysis with evidence-gated quality control
item.description: Cross-species functional MRI analysis requires coordinating specialized workflows and assessing intermediate outputs. We present NeuroImgAgent, a multi-agent platform driven by large language models that translates natural-language requests into workflows for humans, macaques, rats and mice. item.title: Independent Learning after Generative AI Support in School Mathematics: A Systematic Review and Assessment-Stratified Meta-Analysis
item.description: Background and Objective. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) solves school math problems on demand. item.title: Body Form and Architectural Elements for Conservation-Led Daylight Optimization in Cultural Museum: A Case Study of Ikom, Cross River State, Nigeria
item.description: Daylight is a valued architectural resource in museum design, yet uncontrolled daylight exposes cultural artifacts to fading, embrittlement, colour change, ultraviolet degradation, glare, and thermal stress.This exploratory article examines how the body form and architectural elements of a cultural museum in Ikom, Cross River State, Nigeria, can optimize daylight while protecting light-sensitive artifacts.
